basis:
Card carries no tradition/system field; the card frames a May 2012 re-election question whose one stated timing fact is a Mercury retrograde beginning on election day (6 November 2012), decided as Western election astrology. No candidates' charts are supplied on the card; the call rests on incumbency structure plus the stated election-day configuration, confidence reduced, no chart invented.
Reading: an incumbent with a competitive-but-intact polling position (card fact) is the Saturn/continuity side; a Mercury retrograde opening on election day classically signals a messy count, delays and a result that re-runs/confirms the existing state rather than a clean transfer — retrograde periods return to prior decisions. Nothing on the card gives the challenger a decisive configuration.
[Section 8 quantity check] Lines: incumbency plus competitive polling on the card (supporting continuity); election-day Mercury retrograde (supporting a return/confirmation outcome and count confusion, pressing against a clean change); absence of any challenger configuration on the card (no supporting line for Romney). Main line: continuity/incumbency line acting on the outcome. Band: re-election by a workable rather than landslide margin; the retrograde line caps the grade at 'confirmed after a difficult count' rather than 'sweeping win'.
prediction_text: Main call: Barack Obama is re-elected — the incumbent Democrat defeats Mitt Romney in the general election of 6 November 2012. Secondary layer: election day carries a Mercury-retrograde signature, so expect a long, untidy count with disputes over delays and administration of the vote, but the confusion resolves in favour of the sitting president rather than overturning him. Timing fixed by the question: decided 6 November 2012, with the count's untidiness extending some days after. Margin layer: clear but not overwhelming (lower confidence than the winner call).
